jobs.occupation: RE-ADVERTISEMENT - Senior Team Leader for Research Support at the SDU eScience Center for National Research Infrastructure
jobs.description:
We are seeking an experienced Senior Team Leader to lead the Research Support team at the SDU eScience Center. The team plays a central role in helping researchers, research groups, and institutions across Denmark leverage advanced computing, cloud, AI, and data services to accelerate scientific discovery and innovation.

As Senior Team Leader, you will combine scientific insight, technical understanding, and leadership skills to guide a highly skilled team of research support specialists. Working closely with researchers across all disciplines, you will help shape how next-generation digital infrastructure is adopted and utilized within Danish research.

The position offers a unique opportunity to influence both the strategic development of national research services and the day-to-day support provided to tens of thousands of researchers using the center's infrastructure and platforms.

We are looking for a collaborative and forward-looking team leader who is passionate about enabling excellent research through advanced digital technologies. The ideal candidate combines scientific and technical credibility with strong leadership skills and enjoys working at the intersection of research, technology, and service development.

Key responsibilities

• 
Lead and develop the Research Support team, including strategic planning, prioritization, and staff development as part of the management group for the eScience center.

• 
Ensure high-quality support and consultancy services for researchers and customers from the public and private sector using the center's computing, cloud, AI, and data platforms.

• 
Build strong relationships with researchers, departments, external customers, and research infrastructures across SDU and nationally.

• 
Identify emerging research and customers’ needs and contribute to the development of new services, tools, and support initiatives.

• 
Collaborate with the center's technical teams to ensure that infrastructure and services align with user requirements and scientific developments.

Required qualifications

• 
Relevant university degree at Master's level or higher in computer science, engineering, natural sciences, data science, computational science, or a related discipline.

• 
Demonstrated leadership experience, including responsibility for teams, projects, or complex research initiatives.

• 
Strong understanding of computational research, scientific computing, data-intensive research, AI, or digital research infrastructure.

• 
Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills in both Danish and English.

• 
The ability to engage effectively with researchers, technical specialists, customers from the private and public sector.

• 
Proven ability to translate scientific and customers’ needs into practical solutions and service developments.

Desired qualifications

• 
At least 3 years of experience from a university, research organization, national research infrastructure, or technology-oriented organization, including experience leading projects, teams, or research support activities. 

• 
Familiarity with high-performance computing, cloud computing, AI platforms, research data management, or research software engineering.

• 
Experience developing research support services, training activities, or scientific user communities.

• 
Knowledge of the Danish or European research infrastructure landscape.

While the positions offer flexibility and the possibility of remote work, the candidate is expected to be on-site in Odense.

About the SDU eScience Center

The SDU eScience Center is a national center for advanced digital research infrastructure at the University of Southern Denmark. The center develops, operates, and continuously advances large-scale computing, cloud, data, and AI services that support research across all scientific disciplines.

As Denmark's leading provider of research cyberinfrastructure, the center plays a central role in the national ecosystem for research computing and digital services. Through close collaborations with Danish universities, public institutions, and international partners, the center helps researchers access the computational resources and digital platforms needed to address some of society's most complex scientific and technological challenges.

The center is the primary developer and operator of UCloud, Denmark's national research cloud, which provides researchers with seamless access to advanced computing resources, AI and machine learning environments, data-intensive workflows, and scientific applications. Today, the platform serves tens of thousands of users across the Danish research community and forms a key component of the national e-infrastructure landscape.

At the SDU eScience Center, we combine the mindset of a research environment with the professionalism of a modern technology organization. Our teams work at the intersection of cloud computing, high-performance computing, AI infrastructure, data management, software engineering, and digital platform development. We actively contribute to open-source technologies and collaborate closely with researchers to transform emerging technologies into robust services with national impact.

At our center, you will be joining a highly collaborative community where brilliant minds—from IT professionals and data specialists to world-class researchers—converge to drive research innovation. We don’t just maintain servers; we build the foundational digital platforms that empower researchers, students and innovators to solve global challenges. 

Condition of Employment

The starting date for the job is as soon as possible, and it will be agreed with the successful candidate. The appointment is for a full-time permanent position.

All inquiries are welcome. Please contact:

Prof. Director Claudio Pica

SDU eScience center

Dept. of Mathematics and Computer Science

University of Southern Denmark

email: pica@cp3.sdu.dk

Application deadline 28 October 2026.

Employment shall take place in accordance with the framework agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations).

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements.

As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process.

SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary.

Application must include cover letter, CV and certificate. All documents in connection with the application should not contain CPR number (civil registration number) – in that case, the CPR number must be crossed out.

All attached files must be in Adobe PDF format. Cover letter and CV can contain max. 5 Mb.

We recommend that you read how to apply before you apply.

The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

About SDU

The University of Southern Denmark was established to create value for and with society. Whether our contributions come in the form of excellent research, innovative solutions, education or learning, we must make a positive difference to society and contribute to a sustainable future. We do this by cultivating talents and creating the best environments for research and learning. It is therefore crucial that SDU retains, develops and recruits talent. At the same time, we need to ensure consistently high quality in all our activities – and we can only do that with the right people. The University’s researchers, lecturers, students, managers and technical/administrative staff are the foundation of our success.

jobs.occupation: Associate Professor in Radiography
jobs.description:
A position as associate professor (10% time) is vacant at the Research Unit of Radiology (Odense), the Department of Clinical Research, Faculty of Health Sciences, University of Southern Denmark.

UNIFY – Research and Innovation Unit of Radiology, Department of Clinical Research, Faculty of Health Sciences, University of Southern Denmark (SDU), in collaboration with University College Lillebælt (UCL) and Odense Universitetshospital (OUH), invites applications for a position as Associate Professor in Radiography, with 10% research time at the Department of Radiology, OUH. The position is offered for a five-year period with the possibility of extension. The starting date is subject to agreement.

About the research unit

UNIFY – Research and Innovation Unit of Radiology conducts high-quality research across all radiological specialties and contributes significantly to the education and development of highly qualified staff for both clinical and academic work.

The unit values researchers with diverse professional backgrounds and has approximately 20 affiliated members, including a professor, associate professors, PhD students, adjunct professors and others.

The unit has a well-established research environment and organises a number of regular activities and meetings throughout the year, including research retreats combining academic and social activities.

Research and Teaching Responsibilities
The position involves research, academic development, research training, teaching, including examinations, supervision and assessment activities.

Qualifications and Expectations
The Associate Professor must hold a primary position at UCL.

The successful applicant must have documented research and teaching experience within radiography and a particular interest in ultrasound.

Furthermore, strong collaborative skills are required in order to further develop research in radiography, both across disciplines and at national and international level. Having international research collaborators is considered an advantage but is not a requirement.

Joint Research Strategy for the Department of Clinical Research and OUH

The joint research strategy of the Department of Clinical Research and OUH sets the direction for our shared research activities in the coming years.

Based on the vision, “We conduct research together to create the patient care of the future,” particular emphasis is placed on:

• 
Research across disciplines, with people at the centre

• 
Strong research environments as a driving force for development

• 
The research pathway from idea to impact

Further information about the joint research strategy is available on the SDU website.

Applicants Must Document

• 
A PhD degree or equivalent postgraduate research qualifications

• 
Relevant research experience documented through publications in international peer-reviewed journals

• 
Relevant clinical experience

• 
Relevant experience in educational administration

• 
A successful track record in obtaining research funding

Applicants must meet the qualifications required at Associate Professor level in accordance with the applicable Danish Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities.

Reporting

The Associate Professor will report to Head of Research Bo Mussmann on matters relating to the associate professorship.

Contact

For further information about the position, please contact Head of Research Bo Mussmann, Department of Clinical Research/OUH: Email: bo.mussmann@rsyd.dk, Telephone: +45 20 59 88 56

Application deadline

01.11.2026 at 23:59 CET

Salary and terms of employment

The applicant will be employed in accordance with the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations).

The position as Associate Professor is placed within salary steps 4–8 of the state salary scale, depending on seniority. In addition, a centrally agreed associate professor allowance is paid, and further qualification- and function-related allowances may be negotiated.

The work location will be at Kløvervænget 10, 2nd floor, 5000 Odense C, Denmark.  

Application

Applications must be submitted electronically using the link “Apply now” - see below. 

We strongly recommend that you read How to apply for a position at SDU before you apply. 

Only applications written in English will be accepted for evaluation. 

Your application must include the following as PDF files:

Please note that the application (the motivation letter) and CV must not exceed 10 MB in total).

• 
a motivation letter 

• 
a detailed CV 

• 
degree certificates (including a Ph.D.-diploma)

• 
a complete and numbered list of publications 

• 
6 scientific peer-reviewed publications considered by the candidate as most important for this position. Please note that a copy of each publication must be attached as a pdf file. 

• 
It is permitted to merge copies of the selected publications into a single PDF file

• 
a teaching portfolio detailing the candidate’s prior teaching experience, teaching skills, and teaching philosophy

• 
a research plan

• 
a detailed description of research experience 

• 
an explanation of other qualifications relevant to the position

Please note that all the above-mentioned information must be included in the application

Incomplete applications regarding the above-mentioned requirements will not be assessed.

Assessment

Shortlisting will be used as part of the initial selection process. 

Assessment of shortlisted applications will be done under the existing Appointment Order for universities. Shortlisted applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. The committee may request additional information, and, if so, it is the responsibility of the applicant to provide the necessary material. 

When the assessment committee has submitted its report, the applicants will receive part of the evaluation that concerns themselves. 

References will be obtained for the preferred candidate from their current and previous employers. Applicants invited for interview should expect to complete a work-related personality assessment.

Living and working in Denmark

Foreign applicants will be offered Danish language training as part of the employment. 

The International Staff Office (ISO) at SDU provides a variety of services for new employees, guests and people who consider applying for a job at the University of Southern Denmark. 

The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

jobs.occupation: Purchaser - Global Supply Chain
jobs.description:
Do you have experience with technical or project procurement in a larger international company? Would you like to help develop a global supply chain in an international project-driven organization? Then you may be the Purchaser we are looking for.

We are upgrading, servicing, and operating engine- and biomass-based power plants around the world. This creates a continuous need to source goods and services from subcontractors and ensure reliable transport for our customers.

For our Global Supply Chain department, we are looking for an outgoing and internationally minded colleague with commitment, determination, and a positive attitude. The department consists of 20 employees responsible for procurement, warehousing, and transport of goods and services.

BWSC – Ever better energy! 

Join us in our mission of building a world of sustainable energy and make a meaningful impact on the world of power generation and energy conversion.

BWSC is a leading player in the power generation industry, specializing in the service, operations, and maintenance of power plants. We are seeking to always provide Ever Better Energy whether it comes to optimizing a conventional power plant, operating a biomass power plant or constructing new energy facilities. Our commitment to excellence, innovation, and environmental stewardship sets us apart in the industry.

Your responsibilities

• Support Project Procurement Managers with procurement tasks related to the execution of upgrading, service- and maintenance projects for engine and biomass power plants globally.
• Obtain quotations from suppliers and place purchase orders within a defined area of responsibility.
• Participate in broader departmental activities such as category management, supplier relationship development, negotiations, and implementation of supplier agreements.
• Contribute to identifying and evaluating potential suppliers.
• Convert purchase requisitions into purchase orders.
• Maintain and update various data, including supplier data, in the ERP system.
• Follow up on purchase orders, deliveries and invoice approvals.
• Assist with various development-oriented Global Supply Chain tasks within BWSC, including work instructions and new workflows.
The work is carried out in close collaboration with other departments in a dynamic and project-oriented organization. A flexible, cooperative, and positive attitude is therefore essential.

Desired Background and Qualifications

• Experience within procurement, including purchase order placement and follow-up.
• Completed education as an office assistant and/or relevant higher education qualification.
• Minimum 3 years of practical experience with technical or project procurement.
• Strong written and spoken English skills.
• Good IT skills and experience with ERP systems, preferably Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central.
• Ability to work in a structured manner and meet deadlines.
What do we offer? 

At BWSC we build inspiring careers locally and internationally and give you access to a great network of possibilities. 

We offer you a position with great colleagues and the opportunity to bring your skills into play and grow professionally and personally. As a Purchaser at BWSC, you will receive a competitive starting salary and a strong reward package.

We offer an exciting position in a skilled, collaborative, and project-driven work environment, with opportunities for professional development and growth.

We have a good canteen, fitness facilities, and an active Staff Club that organizes various events and activities. Our HQ is located in Allerød, close to the train station and only a 30-minute ride from central Copenhagen.

Ready for a challenge?  

We review applications and invite relevant candidates for interviews on an ongoing basis, so please apply as soon as possible.

If you have any questions regarding the position, please contact Supply Chain Manager Anders S. A. Pedersen at asap@bwsc.dk.

BWSC is committed to promoting equality and diversity. We encourage all qualified candidates to apply, regardless of ethnic background, gender, sexual orientation, disability, religion, or age. Therefore, we do not recommend specifying age, etc., in the application. 

BWSC no longer receives or handles applications received via email due to GDPR requirements. In order for your application to be processed, you must submit your application via our online recruitment system. 

Get to know us even better on our website, www.bwsc.com, where you can learn more about our business, organization, project portfolio, and what we want to achieve at BWSC. 

About BWSC 

Burmeister & Wain Scandinavian Contractor A/S (BWSC) is a global power plant Operation & Maintenance and technical service provider with engineering expertise, enabling power plant owners to deliver cleaner and affordable energy. We are experts in servicing, upgrading, operating, and maintaining energy systems for diesel, natural gas, and renewable baseload power plants worldwide. We help our customers increase reliability and availability of energy production, improve efficiency and performance of their power plant, design and integrate future-proof technologies, and secure lower cost of maintenance.

Our people are at the core of everything we do and key to building strong relationships with our customers. We invest in our people and their wellbeing, supporting professional development and creating an environment where collaboration, knowledge sharing, and personal growth drive our continued success and growth as a company.

jobs.occupation: Sales Executive - Ready to turn Software/ERP expertise into closed deals? Interform HQ Birkerød, DK or Remote
jobs.description:
The role

Interform builds InterformNG2, an Output Management platform that sits next to the ERP and handles the documents a business runs on: invoices, labels, delivery notes, e-invoicing. When output fails, shipments stop and invoices get rejected. Our customers buy certainty that this never happens.

You will sell InterformNG2 to new customers across Europe - with our core markets in the Nordics, Germany and Austria, Benelux and the UK - typically manufacturing, logistics and distribution companies running ERPs such as Infor, SAP, Microsoft Dynamics or IBM i. You own the full sales cycle from first conversation to signed agreement.

There is no BDR team here, but you are not starting from a blank sheet either. We identify the most relevant accounts together, backed by an AI-driven engine that tracks buying signals across our markets. Your job is what happens next: the outreach, the conversations, the proposals and the close.

What you will do

• 
Turn qualified target accounts into meetings, pipeline and closed deals across your European territory.

• 
Open doors through direct outreach and your own network of ERP consultants, partners and IT decision-makers.

• 
Run full sales cycles - qualification, demo coordination, proposal, negotiation, close - in close collaboration with the rest of the commercial team.

• 
Work with our partner ecosystem around Infor, SAP, Microsoft Dynamics, IBM i and other ERP platforms as a second route to market.

• 
Feed what you learn in the market back into how we position and price.

Who you are

• 
Driven. You show up every day ready to do your best, and you keep that standard through long sales cycles.

• 
Connected in the ERP ecosystem. Ecosystem knowledge is essential in this role: you know at least one major ERP ecosystem in real depth - the partners and implementation consultants in it, how they influence a deal and when to bring them in - and you bring a working network you can call on from day one.

• 
Self-starting. You plan your own work, execute without being chased, and deliver.

• 
Accountable. You own your number and you follow up - customers can trust that you are always a step ahead.

• 
At home in the ERP world. You have sold software or services into environments running Infor, SAP, Microsoft Dynamics, IBM i or comparable ERP platforms, and you speak the language of IT managers and operations directors.

• 
AI-forward. You already use AI in your daily sales work - research, preparation, follow-up - and want a company that works the same way.

• 
A closer. You have proven you can turn outreach into pipeline and pipeline into signed deals - not just manage inbound.

• 
Languages: fluent English is required. German, Danish or Dutch on top is a strong advantage - ideally you cover one of our core markets natively.

What we offer

• 
A place in a solid company: profitable, in strong growth, and with a large market still ahead of us.

• 
A product that is easy to stand behind: more than 4,500 installations worldwide, and customers who stay.

• 
A defined category - Output Management - where we compete on depth, not noise.

• 
Short decision paths and direct access to management.

• 
An AI-driven account-based marketing engine that shows you which companies are in the market - so your time goes to conversations, not list-building.

• 
A competitive package that rewards what you close.

About Interform A/S

Interform has built Output Management software since 1987 from our headquarters in Birkerød, Denmark. Our platform, InterformNG2, works with any ERP, any format and any environment - customers change or upgrade their ERP and keep their output running. Our first customer from 1987 is still with us today. Our customer base is international - companies across the Nordics, Germany and Austria, Benelux, the UK and further afield - and our own team works across borders in the same way, with colleagues based in Denmark and Germany. We are a profitable, solidly run company in strong growth, and investment backing supports continued development of the platform.

Upload your CV and cover letter, including the deals you are most proud of.

jobs.occupation: PhD fellowship in Veterinary Virology
jobs.description:
Department of Veterinary and Animal Sciences
 Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences
 University of Copenhagen

   

  We are offering a PhD fellowship in Veterinary Virology commencing 1st of February 2027.

  Our group and research
 Forskningsgruppen udfører forskning og undervisning inden for områderne enzootiske og zoonotiske virusinfektioner hos dyr. Forskningen vil de kommende år fokuseres på influenza infektioner i dyr, med fokus på zoonotiske aspekter af svine influenza virus. Gruppen bestå pt af ca. 20 forskere, phd studerende, studentermedhjælpere og 2 andre labornater. Vi har altid meget travlt, men har et godt arbejdsmiljø med masser af humor, kageklub og fleksible arbejdsopgaver og hvor alle hjælper alle. 

  The research group for Veterinary and Zoonotic Virology consists of around 20 members and as the name states work on both veterinary and zootonic viruses with a main focus on swine influenza A virus. We utilize different molecular methods such viral isolation in cells, qPCR/PCR, sequencing, ELISA and different immunological assays. The research group is very social and we have journal club, cake and breakfast club and Friday bars etc. 

  Project description
 The PhD project will be on cross-reactive vaccines for swine influenza A virus. The first part of the project will be focussed on establishing immunological assays in the laboratory and generating hyperimmune serum in pigs experimentally for following antigenic characterization of Danish swine influenza A virus. The second part of the PhD will be on selecting representative vaccine strains testing them first experimentally in pigs and afterwards in the field.

  Principal supervisor is Professor Lars Erik Larsen, Department of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, lael@sund.ku.dk, phone:  +4540998434

  Start:                  1 February 2027 

  Duration:          3 years as a PhD student

  Job description
 Your key tasks as a PhD student at SUND are:

   	
• Carrying through an independent research project under supervision.    	
• Completing PhD courses or other equivalent education corresponding to approximately 30 ECTS points. 	
• Participating in active research environments including a stay at another research team. 	
• Obtaining experience with teaching or other types of dissemination related to your PhD project 	
• Teaching and disseminating your knowledge. 	
• Writing a PhD thesis on the grounds of your project   PhD Programme Description:
 The PhD programme is a three-year full-time research education within the framework of the 5+3 scheme, intended for candidates holding a relevant academic degree within the project’s subject area (e.g., [relevant degrees]).

  Qualifications:
 If you have completed your academic education in Denmark, the admission to the PhD programme requires a relevant Master’s degree (equivalent to 180 ECTS BSc + 120 ECTS MSc).

  If you have an academic education from abroad, you must have either a degree equivalent to a Danish master's degree (180 ETCS + 120 ECTS MSc), or at a minimum, a bachelor’s degree equivalent to a Danish bachelor's degree (180 ECTS) and be academically qualified at master's level.

  As part of the assessment of whether you meet the educational requirements, you must also achieve a positive academic evaluation and be assessed as the best qualified for the position.

  Other important criteria are:

   	
• The grade point average achieved 	
• Professional qualifications relevant to the PhD project 	
• Previous publications 	
• Relevant work experience 	
• Other professional activities 	
• A curious mind-set with a strong interest in veterinary virology 	
• Language skills   Place of employment
 The place of employment is at the Department of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen. We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in dynamic and international research environment. Our research facilities include modern laboratories and the project will be carried out in collaboration with Statens Serum Institute, Landbrug og Fødevarer and Ceva Animal Health.

  Terms of employment 
 The average weekly working hours are 37 hours per week.

  The position is a fixed-term position limited to a period of 3 years. The start date is 1st of February 2027 or after agreement.

  The employment is conditioned upon the applicant’s successful enrolment as a PhD student at the Graduate School at the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project formulated by the applicant.

  The PhD study must be completed in accordance with The Ministerial Order on the PhD programme (2013) and the Faculty’s rules on achieving the degree. 

  Salary, pension and terms of employment are in accordance with the agreement between the Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. Depending on seniority, the monthly salary starts at approximately 27,800 DKK/Roughly 3,700 EUR (October 2021 level) plus pension.

  You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

  Questions
 For specific information about the PhD fellowship, please contact the principal supervisor.

  General information about PhD studies at the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences is available at the Graduate School’s website: https://healthsciences.ku.dk/phd/guidelines/

  Application procedure
 Your application must be submitted electronically by clicking ‘Apply now’ below. The application must include the following documents in PDF format: 

  1. Motivated letter of application (max. one page)

  2. CV incl. education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position

  3. Certified copy of original Master of Science diploma and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in other language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted. As a prerequisite for a PhD fellowship employment, your master’s degree must be equivalent to a Danish master’s degree. We encourage you to read more in the assessment database: https://ufm.dk/en/education/recognition-and-transparency/find-assessments/assessment-database. Please note that we might ask you to obtain an assessment of your education performed by the Ministry of Higher Education and Science.

  4. Publication list (if possible)

  Application deadline:  [Wednesday 4 November 2026, 23.59pm CET 

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

  The further process 
 After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the hiring committee. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment by an unbiased assessor.

  The assessor makes a non-prioritized assessment of the academic qualifications and experience with respect to the above-mentioned area of research, techniques, skills and other requirements listed in the advertisement.

  Once the assessment work has been completed each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself.

  You find information about the recruitment process at: http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/

  The applicants will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the diversity of society and encourage all qualified candidates to apply regardless of personal background.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral position in computational modeling of visual perception
jobs.description:
The Department of Psychology, Faculty of Health Sciences, University of Southern Denmark (SDU) invites applications for a fully funded postdoctoral position in computational modeling of visual perception. The position is available for up to 36 months and is part of a project led by Dr. Gregory Scott Francis that is supported by the SDU Department of Psychology. The starting date is March 15, 2026, or as soon as possible thereafter.

Research environment

The postdoc will be affiliated with the Research Unit of Health and Cognitive Psychology. The position is at the SDU Esbjerg campus but will also involve interaction with staff at the SDU Odense campus. 

Project description

A basic process of the visual system is to monitor the location and characteristics of objects in a scene, and the multiple object tracking (MOT) paradigm has identified many fundamental aspects of this process. With a rich literature of empirical results, this paradigm is ready for theoretical development, which this project intends to pursue using an integrate-and-fire neural network model known as LAMINART. A key aspect of the model is the ability to select/segment visual objects, which may explain how people can (seemingly) effortlessly track multiple objects in a dynamic visual scene. 

The successful candidate will be required to design, program and analyze an integrate-and-fire neural network model of visual perception. Good programming (Python) skills are required along with a good understanding of empirical methods and ways to connect empirical findings with model behavior. The position also involves teaching duties.

The project involves collaboration with Prof. Søren Krogh Andersen, also at SDU.

Qualifications

Ideally, applicants for the position should satisfy the following requirements:

• 
PhD level in psychology, cognitive (neuro)science, vision science, or a related field

• 
Research experience as evidenced by conference contributions and peer-reviewed journal articles in a field related to the offered position

• 
Expertise in visual attention and perception

• 
Strong analytical skills, including the ability to design, implement, and analyze complex experiments

• 
Be willing and able to teach for the Department of Psychology

• 
Prior experience with neural network modeling is a plus

• 
Prior experience with cognitive modelling is a plus

• 
Good command of statistics

• 
Good command of Python (or similar programming languages and a willingness to learn)

• 
Very good command of the English language in spoken and written form

• 
Some knowledge of the Danish language is a plus

Candidates who are about to obtain these qualifications are also encouraged to apply. 

Contact information

For further information about the position, please contact Dr. Greg Francis, SDU (email: gfrancis@health.sdu.dk; phone: +45 65 50 16 98), or Professor Søren Krogh Andersen (email: skandersen@health.sdu.dk; phone: +45 65 50 49 57)

Application deadline

The application deadline is November 08, 2026, at 23.59 hrs. CET.

Salary and terms of employment

The base salary for a postdoctoral researcher is DKK 36,877.42, with an additional job structure supplement of DKK 5,230.75. This brings the total monthly salary to DKK 42,108.16.

The successful applicant will be employed in accordance with the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations).

Application

Applications must be in English and submitted electronically using the link "Apply now". 

Attached files must be in Adobe PDF format.

We strongly recommend that you read How to apply for a position at SDU before you apply.

The application must include (as PDF files) (please note that the application (the motivation letter) and CV must not exceed 10 MB in total):

• 
A letter of motivation (max. 1 page)

• 
A detailed CV

• 
Master and PhD degree certificates, if available

• 
A complete and numbered list of publications 

• 
Three scientific publications (or preprints) considered to be most important for the advertised position (please note that one file per publication must be submitted)

• 
Contact details of at least two university supervisors or employers who can provide references

If you experience technical problems, you must contact hcm-support@sdu.dk.

Please note that all the above-mentioned information must be included in the application. 

Incomplete applications and applications received after the application deadline will not be considered. 

Shortlisting of applications may be used in the initial selection process.

Living and working in Denmark

Foreign applicants will be offered Danish language training as part of the employment. 

The International Staff Office (ISO) at SDU provides a variety of services for new employees, guests and people who consider applying for a job at the University of Southern Denmark. 

The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.
